statements.statement: total school-related state aid receipts, assessments and charges increased $42,730 between the governor's FY27 budget request and the final signed cherry sheet
Chapter 70 increased $135,915
charter tuition reimbursement went up $116,413
smart growth school reimbursement came in at $160,187, versus zero two years ago
school choice receiving tuition was $5,541, with an open question whether it should count toward the net increase
school choice sending tuition (a charge) was reduced, picking up about $57,000
charter school sending tuition (a charge) increased about $72,000
the superintendent's request for five items (reading specialists, vice principal FTE, Ignite tutoring seats, music teacher FTE) was discussed as totaling about $350,000
town and schools together are realizing more than $100,000 in savings from new health insurance buyout and high-deductible plan options
the superintendent said the primary school reading specialist could be funded out of health insurance savings for FY27
a fully loaded teacher costs over $100,000, given as one reason restoring grade 1-4 positions for class size was not chosen
the total ask under discussion for the special town meeting article was framed as $400,000
the finance committee reserve fund still has $180,000 available to allocate for things that come up
a governor's proposed supplemental budget could add roughly $168,000 more in Chapter 70 aid, based on a per-student calculation
unrestricted general government aid (UGGA) went up about $30,000
veterans benefits and elderly aid together went up about $43,000, combining with UGGA for almost $74,000 on the town side
the net increase across the full cherry sheet, town and school combined, was heard as about 471 (thousand)
the school had to reduce operations by $761,000 or $771,000 to live within the allocation that was proposed
restated that the school department was short by $760,000, $761,000, or $700,000
with the $400,000 in additional funding, the school would still be about $371,000 negative relative to level services

warnings.about: using smart growth reimbursement or other volatile state aid to fund new recurring school positions
warnings.prediction: funding recurring hiring with non-recurring/volatile state aid risks repeating the ESSER-era problem of positions with no funding once the money disappears
smart growth school reimbursement could go back to zero

warnings.about: reliance on cherry sheet state aid for the budget
warnings.prediction: cherry sheet state aid has been cut mid-year in serious financial crisis years historically (e.g. 2008-2009)

warnings.about: the school budget shortfall carrying forward
warnings.prediction: the town will need to make up the remaining $371,000 shortfall, plus inflationary increases, the following year
